Recently I started traveling cross country by motorcycle for fun. I usually bring a gym bag with clothes, toiletries and some books along with a backpack where I carry some misc tools. Oh, and a .22lr handgun. On the very bottom of my backpack I keep a padlock for those times I stay in a hostel and use their locker.

So I've been riding for over 9 hours and its around midnight when I start to get exhausted. I've been avoiding interstates in favor of the more scenic highways, which also tend to have less traffic. So I decide it's safer to pull over and get some rest. I park in a small ditch, make my way up into some trees for cover and lay out some plastic sheets to lay on. I also put out my jacket for a pillow and my handgun for, you know, just in case. I insert the mag, chamber a round and de-cock the hammer. This means in order to fire the gun I would have to physically pull back the hammer with my thumb and then pull the trigger, at least for the first shot. After passing out for about 8 hours I wake up feeling like I'm terribly late for something even though I have nowhere to be for another 3 weeks. In a rush I pack up my stuff including removing the mag from my gun and throwing it in the backpack. Four hours later I stop for some food feeling tired and sore. The place is empty except for the lady behind the counter and me. After ordering I lazily take off my backpack and drop it it--BOOM!!

What the fuck was that?! Both of us have this scared shitless look and she asks what that was. It felt like minutes before I answered. "Uh, it mustve been the lock on my bag slamming onto the tile floor, sorry. >.> <.< :D" She nervously starts cleaning some things near the phone. I check myself for holes, stuff the food in my bag and get the fuck out there. A couple of miles down the road I pull over and check my bag, yep, forgot to empty the bullet that was chambered. When I dropped the bag it landed on the hammer, shoving the firing pin and setting off the bullet.

Tldr; I accidentally almost robbed a store.
